EVs And Hybrids Push Gas-Only Cars Below Half Of Global Sales

# EVs And Hybrids Push Gas-Only Cars Below Half Of Global Sales

By Jon Markman,

Contributor.

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights.

 Analyzing tech stocks through the prism of cultural change.

Oct 15, 2026, 11:26am EDT

## Summary

Gasoline-only cars lost their global majority for the first time in the first half of 2026, making up 49% of worldwide new-vehicle sales according to Mobility Global data. During this period, global car sales fell by about 5%, but gasoline-only sales dropped by 10% to 20.25 million vehicles. Meanwhile, battery-electric and hybrid car sales grew despite the shrinking market. Battery-electric cars reached 6.87 million sales, and hybrids reached 7.27 million sales. In the European Union, battery-electric sales rose 45% in the first eight months of 2026, matching gasoline cars with a 21.7% market share each.
